items.title: FDA warns Chinese providers of compounding APIs over record-request refusals
items.snippet: Neither Chongqing Qiancan Technology nor Tianjin Healthcare Medical Technology provided the records requested by the FDA, leading the agency to issue import alerts and warning letters.

items.title: PepGen shares almost double as DM1 oligonucleotide achieves ‘best in class’ splicing
items.snippet: Mean splicing correction for PepGen’s PGN-EDODM1 was 46.5% at week 13, compared to under 30% for competitors like Dyne Therapeutics, Novartis and Ionis Pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Capricor parts ways with 10% of staff as FDA decision on DMD cell therapy nears
items.snippet: Awaiting a decision on Nov. 22 for its embattled Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy deramiocel, Capricor has reduced its workforce by 10% and slowed programs not directly related to deramiocel, the biotech revealed in its third quarter earnings report.

items.title: Capricor ramps up manufacturing spend ahead of FDA decision for DMD therapy
items.snippet: Less than two weeks away from a highly anticipated FDA ruling on its cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, Capricor Therapeutics has reported increased investment in its San Diego plant to support commercial production.

items.title: NextCure nixes staffers before proposed merger
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Novartis’ Zolgensma woes, BIO’s China plan, GLP-1s’ new safety warning, FDA’s stacked November
items.snippet: Novartis confirms that nine patients treated with its spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy Zolgensma have developed tumors; the FDA orders GLP-1 drugmakers to add a warning to their labels about the risk of a rare eye condition that can lead to vision loss; and the agency is set to decide on no fewer than 11 therapies...

items.title: China has a clear shot to 2030 goals, though economic, cultural barriers remain
items.snippet: To grow into a biopharma juggernaut, China aims to become the leading source of innovative medicines on the global markets—a goal that experts say the country is on track to hit.

items.title: Without US action on China’s innovation blitz, biotech leaders see a Rust Belt future
items.snippet: Policy uncertainty is hampering the growth of U.S. biotech as China rises thanks to carefully planned investment in the industry, experts said during a BioSpace webinar.

items.title: FDA's rare disease framework faces its first real test in Capricor’s DMD drug
items.snippet: Last month, the FDA committed to designing a "fit-for-purpose" framework for regulating rare disease therapies based on patient need and realistically attainable evidence. With the upcoming decision for Capricor’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy deramiocel, this paradigm faces its first key test.

items.title: Coherus cuts 30% of staffers, Gyre makes post-acquisition layoffs
items.snippet: Coherus is narrowing its pipeline projects while Gyre reorganizes after an acquisition, with both biotechs conducting workforce reductions.

items.title: BIO pitches US plan to beat China in biotech ‘space race’
items.snippet: The seven proposals in the Bio Advance plan include easing clinical trial starts, boosting manufacturing and establishing a new White House office to coordinate the government’s biotech policy.

items.title: Beam preps FDA run for industry-first base-edited therapy after pivotal sickle cell success
items.snippet: Beam Therapeutics' risto-cel provided at least 12 consecutive months of freedom from severe pain crises for patients with sickle cell disease in a mid-stage trial, setting the stage for an FDA application as early as this year.

items.title: Bayer wins first-in-class FDA nod for blood thinner, setting stage for BMS-J&J rival
items.snippet: Bayer’s Sunharbo has secured the first FDA approval of its class, establishing a regulatory pathway for other factor XIa inhibitors, such as Bristol Myers Squibb and Johnson and Johnson’s milvexian.

items.title: Delix raises $100M to advance at-home psychedelic without hallucinogenic effects
items.snippet: The series C raise, co-led by Johnson & Johnson’s venture capital arm, will help Delix Therapeutics push its novel psychedelic asset into mid-stage development for major depressive disorder.

items.title: Altimmune gears up for FDA meeting on pivotal Phase 3 trial in alcohol use disorder
items.snippet: Having linked its glucagon/GLP-1 candidate to a significant reduction in heavy drinking days, Altimmune is preparing to speak to the FDA in December about the design of a Phase 3 program.

items.title: BioSpace 2027 Best Places to Work shines light on most admired employers
items.snippet: The list honors 50 life sciences employers of choice. Employees at SERB Pharmaceuticals and CSL Behring share why their companies stand out.

items.title: FDA orders class-wide GLP-1 label update to include potential risk for rare eye disease
items.snippet: Twelve marketed drugs, including Eli Lilly’s and Novo’s weight loss mega-blockbusters, will require a label change under the new FDA update.

items.title: Boehringer, Zealand’s obesity drug doesn’t elevate heart risk in key late-stage test
items.snippet: The Phase 3 results help clarify the safety profile of Zealand and Boehringer Ingelheim’s survodutide, but analysts do not think the drug will find utility beyond patients with liver-related risk factors.

items.title: Lilly to seek second sleep apnea approval after Foundayo reduces disease severity in Phase 3
items.snippet: If approved, the oral GLP-1 would be Eli Lilly’s second marketed drug for obstructive sleep apnea after the GIP/GLP-1 injectable Zepbound secured the first approval in the space in December 2024.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
